protocol.status: Exploratory diagnostic protocol, saved before any diagnostic trajectory was run. It targets two already-known disagreements, so it is outcome-conditioned and cannot be confirmatory.
protocol.target: Unloaded robot, nominal fixed LQR, zero initial tilt, 0.5 N m torque limit, +/-18.2 N pulse from 2.0 to 2.2 s. The planar model recovers; native-contact MuJoCo falls (archived to 0.0625 ms).
protocol.question: Which modelling assumption moves the native fall boundary relative to the planar one: the additional chassis pitch inertia, the unsettled contact start, or the contact and friction model?
protocol.primary: Critical-force bracket per variant: bisection on positive force inside [17.0, 19.5] N, 12 halvings (final width about 0.0006 N), label = fallen or not fallen at 10 s. Reported as the shift of the bracket midpoint from the planar reference.
protocol.secondary: Outcome labels at +18.2 and -18.2 N at both physics steps; state at pulse onset; sampled wheel slip, friction utilisation and normal force; required traction coefficient computed from the planar trajectory.
protocol.bisection_assumption: One fall transition inside the bracket. Checked, not assumed, by 0.01 N scans of 18.10-18.30 N in the planar and unmodified native models. A variant with no transition in the bracket is reported as such.

protocol.interpretation: Each variant changes one declared assumption (the combined variant changes three). A variant that moves the native bracket onto the planar one identifies a sufficient explanation for these two cases only. Nothing is fitted: no variant replaces the archived model, and no parameter is selected because it restores agreement.
protocol.limits: Illustrative parameters; no hardware. A sub-0.1 N boundary shift is far below any plausible physical calibration uncertainty, so the diagnosis concerns simulator assumptions, not robot behaviour.
